name: Mercosur Residency Agreement (Acordo de Residência do Mercosul)

requirement_groups.name: Nationality-based, no job offer or economic test required

requirements.blocker_text: Requires nationality of Argentina, Bolivia, Chile, Colombia, Ecuador, Paraguay, Peru, or Uruguay -- the Mercosur member and associated states covered by Decreto nº 6.975/2009 -- or having naturalised in one of those countries more than 5 years before applying. Nationality is the entire qualifying test: no job offer, sponsor, or minimum-income requirement applies.

Requires a valid passport, criminal-record certificate, and proof of the qualifying nationality; the request can be filed at a Brazilian consulate abroad (VITEM XIII) or, for those already in Brazil, directly with the Federal Police.

evidence_required.document: Criminal-record certificate from the country of origin

outcome.duration_length: 2 years temporary, convertible to indefinite-term residence 90 days before expiry

sources.title: Polícia Federal (gov.br/pf) -- Acordo de Residência do MERCOSUL, listing the 8 qualifying nationalities and the 2-year temporary to indefinite-term conversion process

Ministério da Justiça e Segurança Pública (gov.br/mj) -- news release confirming 64,815 temporary visas/residence authorisations granted Jan 2023-Aug 2024 under the Mercosur agreement and the CPLP portaria combined, with 63,071 of those under the Mercosur agreement specifically

notes: STRUCTURAL FINDING, the single most distinctive route in the Brazil build: nationality alone is the entire qualifying test -- no job offer, employer sponsor, minimum income, or economic activity of any kind is required, a genuinely different mechanism from every other route in this dataset except Poland's Karta Polaka and Korea's F-4 (both ancestry-based rather than current-nationality-based). Classified as 'settled' rather than 'ancestry' since the qualifying test is the applicant's own current nationality, not descent from a national of the destination country -- a meaningful category distinction from Poland's or Korea's ancestry routes, closer in spirit to EU freedom-of-movement-style regional-bloc mobility than to a diaspora-return programme. Real, large-scale, and recently reported: gov.br/mj's own October 2024 news release states 63,071 of 64,815 total grants under this pathway and the related CPLP (Portuguese-speaking-country) arrangement between January 2023 and August 2024 came through the Mercosur agreement specifically, with Bolivia the single largest source country (25,411 registrations) -- this is a genuinely high-volume, well-used route, not a marginal legal curiosity, and the scale itself is tier-1 sourced rather than asserted. A closely related but narrower CPLP (Comunidade dos Países de Língua Portuguesa) arrangement grants similar simplified treatment specifically to Portuguese-speaking-country nationals under Portaria Interministerial MJSP/MRE nº 40/2023 -- not modeled as its own separate route file here given significant overlap with this route's mechanism and with br_naturalisation's own Portuguese-speaking-country naturalisation track (Article 65's constitutional provision, reduced to 1 year residence), but flagged as a candidate for a future dedicated file if this dataset is expanded further. pr_after_months (24) reflects the 2-year temporary-to-indefinite-term conversion this route's holders can request. citizenship_after_months is left honestly null rather than guessed: br_naturalisation's ordinary track requires 4 years of indefinite-term residence (residência por prazo indeterminado), and it is not conclusively established in this research pass whether that 4-year clock starts running from this route's initial 2-year temporary grant or only from the point of conversion to indefinite-term status -- if the former, total time to citizenship eligibility could be as low as 4 years from initial entry; if the latter, it could run to roughly 6 years (2 to convert plus 4 more). Rather than assert either figure without confirming Brazil's specific rule on this point, the gap is flagged here for a follow-up session to resolve against a primary gov.br/mj source.
